items.s: In which district is Nagarjunakonda located?
items.x:
Guntur district was split in April 2022 — Nagarjunakonda (Macherla area) is now in Palnadu district (general knowledge, not checked)
Nagarjunakonda (Ikshvaku capital Vijayapuri) is listed under Guntur district; Nalgonda only shares the Nagarjuna Sagar dam (now Palnadu district, carved out of Guntur in 2022).

items.s: 'Nagarjuna Konda' is located in the district of
items.x:
Guntur district was split on 4 Apr 2022 — Nagarjunakonda is now in Palnadu district (AP district reorganisation; Wikipedia 'Nagarjunakonda').
Nagarjunakonda (Vijayapuri of the Ikshvakus) lies in Macherla mandal on the right bank of the Krishna, in Guntur district (now Palnadu), not in Nalgonda, which holds only the Nagarjuna Sagar dam's left side.

items.s: Which river was the lifeline of Pandya state?
items.x: The Pandya heartland around Madurai lies on the Vaigai, printed here as 'Vengi'; the Godavari, Krishna and Tungabhadra are Deccan rivers.

items.s: The first Gupta ruler to assume the title of ‘Parama Bhagawat’ was
items.x:
Most books and the UPPSC official key give Chandragupta II, who used 'Parama Bhagavata' widely on coins and inscriptions. The NextGen Rocket Sheet gives Samudragupta, styled so in the Nalanda and Gaya copper plates (whose genuineness is doubted).
Samudragupta is the first Gupta styled Paramabhagavata, in his Nalanda and Gaya copper plates (NextGen Rocket); Chandragupta II used it regularly on coins and inscriptions, which is why some keys give him.

items.s: The first Gupta ruler to assume the title of “Param Bhagavata” was
items.x:
Most books and the UPPSC official key give Chandragupta II, who used 'Parama Bhagavata' widely on coins and inscriptions. The NextGen Rocket Sheet gives Samudragupta, styled so in the Nalanda and Gaya copper plates (whose genuineness is doubted).
The Nalanda and Gaya copper plates style Samudragupta Paramabhagavata, making him the first Gupta with the title (NextGen Rocket). The official UPPSC key gave Chandragupta II, who used it widely on coins.

items.x: The Ramappa tank and temple at Palampet were built in 1213 by Recherla Rudra during Ganapatideva's reign, so the pond belongs to Ganapatideva's time. Rudradeva, Mahadeva and Prataparudra are wrong.

items.s: The person who defeated Prataparudra-II and took him captive?
items.x: In the final invasion of 1323 Ulugh Khan defeated Prataparudra II and took him captive; he drowned himself in the Narmada on the way to Delhi. Malik Kafur's 1309-10 siege ended in a treaty.

items.s: The troops raised by the Emperor but not paid directly by the state and placed under the charge of Mansabadars were known as
items.x: Dakhili troops were raised and paid by the state but placed under mansabdars. Walashahi (Balashahi) was the emperor's bodyguard.

items.s: Who was the chief Architect of Taj Mahal?
items.x:
Most books and keys: Ustad Isa. Strictly: Ustad Ahmad Lahori was the principal architect (PMF Art & Culture 04 p.6; modern scholarship); Ahmad Lahori is not among the options.
Many books and keys name 'Ustad Isa' as the Taj's chief architect, so the key is Ustad (Khalil) Isa; modern scholarship credits Ustad Ahmad Lahori (from his son Lutfullah Muhandis's writings), with Isa at most a draftsman.

items.s: Who built the fort at Machilipatnam in 1611?
items.x:
Printed answer: the Dutch (who fortified Masulipatnam from 1605). The year 1611 fits only the English factory (Globe, Hippon); no source dates a fort there to 1611.
1611 is the year the English (British) set up their factory at Machilipatnam after the Globe arrived. The Dutch had been there since 1605 and fortified their factory, so 'Dutch' fits the word 'fort' but not the year.

items.s: Who was the founder of the Radhaswami Satsang, a sect born out of Sikkim in 1851?
items.x: Shiv Dayal Singh, a Khatri (Soamiji Maharaj), founded the Radhasoami Satsang at Agra (1861) – the stem's 'Sikkim, 1851' is garbled; the other names are unrelated.

items.s: The Tamil language weekly ____, founded in May 1924, became the organ of the Self-Respect Movement.
items.x: Kudi Arasu, the Tamil weekly of Periyar, became the organ of the Self-Respect Movement (PMF: Periyar started Kudi Arasu, Puratchi and Viduthalai). (Its launch is usually dated May 1925.)

items.s: At Which session of Indian National Congress, the resolution on Fundamental Rights and Economic Policy was adopted?
items.x: The resolution on Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme was passed at Karachi under Vallabhbhai Patel – in March 1931 ('1930' in the option is a misprint; no session was held in 1930).

items.s: Mahatma Gandhi presided over the Annual Session of Congress only once at: nown as:
items.x: Gandhi presided only at Belgaum; the session was in December 1924 (the option's 1925 is a misprint), so it is still the intended answer.

items.s: On which date was the famous "Dandi March" completed?
items.x: The Dandi March (12 March – 6 April 1930) reached Dandi on 5 April and culminated in breaking the salt law on 6 April 1930.

items.s: In 1964, Neelam Sanjiva Reddy joined Lal Bahadur Shastri's government as Union Minister with which portfolio?
items.x: After resigning over the Kurnool bus-routes verdict, Neelam Sanjiva Reddy joined Shastri's cabinet in 1964 as Union Minister of Steel and Mines (the 'Iron and Mines' option); he was not given Home or Finance.

items.s: Which Maoist leader was killed by security forces in 2012?
items.x: Kishanji (Mallojula Koteswara Rao, from Peddapalli) was killed by security forces in West Bengal in November 2011 (the stem says 2012). Charu Majumdar died in custody in 1972, Kanu Sanyal died in 2010, Veerappan was a brigand.
